report.summary: Two separate causes. The two add-book UI tests fail because the test page object clicks a test id (add-books) that the template does not render (add-book), so they never reach the app; fix that locator first. The API ownership test and the new-user empty-state test both see another user's books, which points to the leak_books defect in list_books (app/main.py:163-166); that is a product bug, so investigate it after the locator fix.

causes.title: Page object clicks a test id that the books template does not render
causes.explanation: BooksPage.add() clicks get_by_test_id("add-books"), but the template's submit button is data-testid="add-book". Playwright waits for a locator that never exists and times out after 5 s before any app behaviour is exercised. The same mismatch breaks both add-book UI tests. The app is correct here; the test support code is wrong. Once the locator matches, test_future_year_shows_error_and_keeps_input still depends on the year validation: with the year_off_by_one defect enabled, next year would be accepted and that test would fail for a real reason.
evidence: tests\ui\test_books_ui.py:13 ... tests\support\pages.py:44 in add -> Locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for get_by_test_id("add-books")
tests\ui\test_books_ui.py:42 (test_future_year...) fails with the same call log waiting for get_by_test_id("add-books")
causes.suggested_fix: Change tests/support/pages.py:44 to get_by_test_id("add-book") (or rename the template attribute to add-books on one side only, and keep both sides consistent). Then rerun both UI tests.

causes.title: Books of other users are returned to the current user (leak_books defect path active)
causes.explanation: list_books() has a branch under "leak_books" in BUGS that runs SELECT * FROM books with no owner filter, so every user's books are listed. This one function feeds both GET /api/books and the /books page render (render_books calls list_books), so the API ownership test sees another user's book id, and a brand-new user's bookshelf shows a book created by another test ('From API-d19d31c9', author Robot). The correct behaviour is owner-scoped listing, so the failing tests are right to fail. Caveat: the workflow file does not set BUGS, so the defect must be enabled in the environment that ran this build; confirm where BUGS is set. Even if it is intentional seeding, these tests fail every time it is on.
evidence: app/main.py:163-164: if "leak_books" in BUGS: rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id").fetchall()
app/main.py:166: else: ... WHERE owner_id = ? ORDER BY id
tests/api/test_books_api.py:41-42: other_ids = [b["id"] for b in other_api.list_books().json()]; assert book["id"] not in other_ids  ->  assert 2 not in [1, 2]

tests\ui\test_login_ui.py:14: expect(books.empty_state).to_be_visible() -> Actual value: None, element(s) not found; aria snapshot of fresh user's page shows row "From API-d19d31c9 Robot Delete" in the table
app/templates/books.html:29-30: empty-state only renders when the books list is empty
causes.suggested_fix: Remove the leak_books branch from list_books() (or make sure BUGS is unset for the CI app run), then rerun the API and login tests. Add a regression check that a new user's /api/books is empty while another user owns books.
